name: VARoleSecretarySessionSchedulingConflict

custom.system_prompt: Greta, Odalys, and Ingmar resolve a scheduling conflict between two conference sessions competing for the same room and time slot. Odalys invites Sigma to keep track of decisions. They agree to move one session, but don't say who will notify the affected speaker. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about that.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Conference room, hybrid meeting, mild urgency

initial_prompt: Generate a conference organizing meeting where Greta, Odalys, and Ingmar resolve a scheduling conflict — two sessions were accidentally booked in the same room at the same time. Odalys invites Sigma to keep track of decisions at the start. The group discusses options normally, Sigma silent. They agree to move one session to a different room, but don't say who will actually notify the affected speaker. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about that. Keep every line short and natural.

variations.context: Conference organizing meeting resolving a room double-booking, with a vague notification commitment

setting.relationship_dynamic: Conference organizers fixing a scheduling mistake together
setting.background: The double-booking was just discovered and the conference is close, adding urgency

scenario_template.topic: Odalys invites Sigma to keep track of decisions from this scheduling-conflict meeting, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, keep track of what we decide here — we need to fix this fast.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: The group confirms the double-booking and discusses which session is easier to move to a different room, Sigma silent.
scenario_template.note: Ordinary organizing content, no need for Sigma yet.

scenario_template.topic: Greta and Ingmar agree to move the smaller session to a different room, but neither says who will notify the affected speaker.
scenario_template.note: This is exactly the incomplete commitment Sigma should catch.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks a small, single clarifying question about who will notify the affected speaker about the room change.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Who's telling the speaker about the room change?' One short question only.

scenario_template.topic: Odalys volunteers to email the speaker right after the meeting, Greta confirms, and the group moves on, Sigma silent again.
scenario_template.note: The group names the actual owner.

scenario_template.topic: Greta wraps the meeting and Sigma gives a brief summary of the room change and who is notifying the speaker.

variations.context: Resolving dual workshop booking conflict at marketing summit.

setting.relationship_dynamic: Conference organizers fixing a scheduling mistake together
setting.background: Two marketing workshops scheduled simultaneously in one space.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma is invited to document decisions in the scheduling-conflict discussion.
The group confirms both workshops are in the same room and debates which can move.
scenario_template.note: Ensure lively discussion, no decision yet.

scenario_template.topic: They decide the advanced marketing workshop can move but don't assign the notification.
scenario_template.note: Agree on change but omit speaker notification plan.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks who will inform the workshop leader about the room change.
One of them offers to contact the leader, another confirms, and they continue planning.
scenario_template.note: Volunteer to email, confirmed, move on quickly.

scenario_template.topic: After agreeing, one wraps up, Sigma reviews the room switch and notification.
scenario_template.note: Sigma summarizes room change and notification plan.

variations.context: Sorting out clashing sales demo bookings at an expo.

setting.relationship_dynamic: Conference organizers fixing a scheduling mistake together
setting.background: Two sales demos are scheduled for the same venue slot.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma is requested to keep a record of resolutions in the session conflict.
scenario_template.note: Invite Sigma to note down decisions.

scenario_template.topic: The group recognizes the overlap and considers which demo to relocate.
scenario_template.note: Discuss pros and cons of moving each, no decisions yet.

scenario_template.topic: They conclude the smaller demo will relocate, without notifying the presenter yet.
scenario_template.note: Decision reached but no mention of informing someone.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks who should contact the demo leader regarding the change.
scenario_template.note: Sigma seeks clarification on the contact person.

scenario_template.topic: Someone takes responsibility to update the demo leader, another acknowledges, proceed.
scenario_template.note: Assign notification duty, confirmed, moving forward.

scenario_template.topic: Following the agreement, one concludes, Sigma recaps the room change and contact.
scenario_template.note: Sigma wraps up with details on room and notification.

user1.name: Odalys
user1.role: Sharp, opinionated, a little impatient committee member, invites Sigma to track decisions. Speaks in short sentences.

user2.name: Greta
user2.role: Organized event planner, proposes the room-swap fix, volunteers to confirm the swap. Speaks in short sentences.

user3.name: Ingmar
user3.role: Calm, deliberate committee member, agrees to the room swap. Speaks in short sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Secretary. Invited once at the start, stays silent through ordinary discussion, and asks one small clarifying question only when the notification commitment lacks an owner. Gives a brief end-of-meeting summary.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
Sigma stays silent through ordinary discussion
Sigma speaks only to ask one small clarifying question when the notification commitment lacks an owner
Every line is short and natural
The meeting ends with a brief Sigma summary of the fix and who is notifying the speaker
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not weigh in on which session should move
The group decides everything; Sigma only remembers
